heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 handles Polymaker PolyMax PETG natively with its stock stainless steel nozzle, requiring no enclosure. Tuned for a maximum volumetric flow of 14 mm³/s, it reliably reaches safe sustained print speeds up to 167 mm/s at standard 0.2mm layer heights.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with a thin layer of PVP glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Max Volumetric Speed at 14 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent under-extrusion at high linear toolhead speeds.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' set to 2.0 mm to cleanly shear molten PolyMax PETG and minimize fine hair stringing.
Set outer wall speed to 120 mm/s and inner wall speed to 160 mm/s to ensure consistent surface gloss and strong layer bonding without exceeding the volumetric flow limit.
Set fan trip threshold under 'Layer time cooling' to keep fans at 20% on layers >12s, ramping up to 50% only on overhangs and bridges.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine cobwebbing across travel paths
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PolyMax PETG is hygroscopic and exhibits low melt viscosity when moisture is absorbed or when unretracted filament oozes.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament at 65°C for 6-8 hours, enable 'Avoid crossing perimeters', and set retraction distance to 0.8 mm with 35 mm/s retraction speed.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Bed adhesion failure or PEI surface tearing
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG bonds aggressively to bare PEI surfaces causing damage on removal, or poor first-layer squish due to oil contamination.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a thin layer of liquid glue or glue stick as a release barrier, set the bed temperature to 75°C, and decrease first layer speed to 35 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak interlayer bonding and brittle part fractures
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling fan speeds chilling the extruded track before molecular polymer chains interdiffuse.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Reduce cooling fan speed to 20% minimum and 50% maximum, and bump the printing nozzle temperature to 245°C.

faq.question: Does Polymaker PolyMax PETG require a hardened steel nozzle upgrade on the Bambu Lab A1?
faq.answer: No. PolyMax PETG is a non-abrasive polymer blend containing no carbon or glass fibers, making it completely safe to print on the A1 stock stainless steel nozzle.

faq.question: Can I print PolyMax PETG at the Bambu Lab A1 default 300+ mm/s speeds?
faq.answer: No. The melt flow of this material is capped at roughly 14 mm³/s on the A1 hotend, which mechanically limits safe, defect-free printing to 167 mm/s at standard 0.2mm layer heights.

faq.question: Why is glue stick necessary on the Bambu Textured PEI plate for PETG?
faq.answer: PETG molecularly fuses with PEI coating at typical 75°C bed temps; the glue acts as a sacrificial release agent to prevent tearing off chunks of the PEI coating when removing parts.

faq.question: Is an enclosure required to print PolyMax PETG on the Bambu Lab A1?
faq.answer: No, PolyMax PETG has very low thermal shrinkage compared to ABS or ASA, making it ideally suited for the open-bed Bambu Lab A1 without warping issues.
